trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Premiums, deductibles and Medicare Part B charges are set a year ahead and are rising 6–10% a year into 2027 (family employer premium $28,303 in 2026; ACA filings +15% median for 2027; per-capita spending $17,496 in 2026 to $22,095 in 2031), so health costs show up as smaller raises, bigger paycheck deductions and skipped care.

Expiry of enhanced ACA subsidies (2026) and Medicaid work/community-engagement rules (2027–28) push the uninsured from 28.6 million (2025) to about 33 million by 2028; insurers exit exchanges and trim Medicare Advantage, so people lose plans, doctors and continuity, and hospitals absorb uncompensated care.

trends.trend: GLP-1s, new drugs and government price-setting
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Obesity drugs become a mass consumer product (pills at $149–299 cash, $50 Medicare copay to end-2027, list price cut to $675 in 2027) while Medicare-negotiated prices arrive on fixed dates (2026, 2027, 2028) and next-generation drugs (retatrutide, CagriSema) reach approval – changing bodies, pharmacy counters and what a prescription costs.

trends.trend: Ageing, Medicare strain and slow longevity gains
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: The last baby boomers turn 65 in 2029, Medicare enrollment passes 75 million by 2030, the hospital trust fund is projected to deplete in 2033, and official life-expectancy assumptions barely move – more retirees, higher premiums, crowded clinics and a looming benefit-cut debate.

trends.trend: AI and workforce strain in care delivery and administration
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: AI is arriving first in billing, coding, prior authorisation and back offices (payers and pharma book AI-linked restructurings; employers blame AI-enabled billing for higher claims) and in 1,600+ FDA-authorised devices, against a clinician shortage – patients meet more software and fewer staff, and nobody in the official forecasts has priced it.

accuracy.why: Prices are in signed agreements backed by statute: a manufacturer that walks away faces the IRA excise tax or exit from Medicare/Medicaid, and CMS is legally bound to publish and apply the MFP (T1). They are set adversarially through offers, counteroffers and three meetings per company, and the programme has been litigated by manufacturers in multiple circuits (T2). The mechanism reaches 2028 with drugs already selected and later cycles fixed in statute (T4, T5). No directional forecast bias – the residual risk is legal/political (court rulings, orphan-drug carve-outs added by the 2025 'Working Families Tax Cuts' law, MFN side deals), not estimation error. No scored track record is needed (T3 n/a).

sources.what_it_forecasts: Traded probabilities for dated health events: FDA approval of retatrutide (0.70 before 2028), CagriSema (~0.89 before 2027), ACA tax-credit extension (0.31–0.33 before 2028), a new pandemic (0.15–0.16 before 2028), a type 1 diabetes cure by 2033, measles counts.
sources.horizon: mostly to end-2027; a few contracts to 2029–2033

latest_edition.title: Kalshi and Polymarket open health markets, API snapshot

accuracy.why: Real money (T1), many independent traders (T2) and every contract is resolved and scored, with public calibration studies of both venues (T3). Horizon fit is weak: liquid contracts end within ~14 months and the multi-year ones are thin (e.g. about $11k volume on the 2033 diabetes-cure market), where long-shot bias and capital lock-up distort prices. No T5.

richness.why: A probability per named event and date plus resolution rules; no reasoning. 212 Kalshi market rows and 54 Polymarket rows saved.

ai.why: Live prices dated 2026-11-18 that can re-price on AI news, but no health contract isolates AI (searched event titles: none on AI diagnostics, AI drug approvals or clinician displacement).

ai_evidence.search_note: Searched 20,667 open Kalshi event titles and Polymarket search results for health keywords; no health-specific AI contract found. Metaculus API returned 403 ('only available to authenticated users').

sources.why_top_or_not: Highest structural accuracy for a handful of dated binaries (drug approvals, subsidy extension, pandemic), but too sparse and short-dated to carry a scenario; best used as probability checks on the top sources.

sources.publisher: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation / The Lancet
covers_trends: Ageing, Medicare strain and slow longevity gains
sources.what_it_forecasts: Life expectancy, healthy life expectancy and cause-specific burden for 204 countries to 2050 under a reference and alternative risk-elimination scenarios (global life expectancy 73.6 in 2022 to 78.1 in 2050).

latest_edition.title: Burden of disease scenarios for 204 countries and territories, 2022–2050: a forecasting analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021

sources.update_cadence: irregular (2018, 2024); a GBD 2023 forecasting paper was not found as of 2026-11-18

accuracy.why: Peer-reviewed with out-of-sample validation reported in the paper, and demographic momentum does much of the work (T5), but no stakes, no adversarial market, and no published record of how earlier IHME forecasts fared (its COVID-19 projections were heavily criticised). Journal publication date from citation; not printed in the repository copy.

richness.why: Country-by-country life expectancy and burden tables with risk-factor scenarios; no named events, firms or prices.

ai.why: Latest forecasting edition is May 2024 and has no AI treatment (the 12 keyword hits are 'ambient air pollution').

ai_evidence.search_note: Searched 54-page paper: 12 hits, all 'ambient' (air pollution/temperature); no AI, machine learning or automation as a health driver.

sources.why_top_or_not: The well-known global longevity forecast, explicitly scored low: pre-2025, unincentivised and silent on AI and GLP-1s.
